record.original_question: Describe a mechanical or fluid model whose configuration space is D_mu(M) and whose kinetic energy defines an L2 left-invariant metric, and identify whether any physically meaningful systems realize this type of invariance.

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Describe a model for an L2 left-invariant metric on the group Dµ (M ). Are there any interesting physical systems demonstrating that type of invariance?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a closed oriented Riemannian manifold with Riemannian volume form $\mu$, and let $D_\mu(M)$ denote the group of smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$, regarded as an infinite-dimensional Lie group with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{X}_\mu(M)$ of smooth divergence-free vector fields. The $L^2$ inner product on $\mathfrak{X}_\mu(M)$ is
$$\langle u,v\rangle_{L^2} = \int_M g(u,v)\,\mu.$$
Extending this inner product by left translations yields a left-invariant weak Riemannian metric on $D_\mu(M)$: for $\eta \in D_\mu(M)$ and tangent vectors $U,V \in T_\eta D_\mu(M)$,
$$\langle U,V\rangle_\eta^{\text{left}} = \langle (TL_{\eta^{-1}})U,(TL_{\eta^{-1}})V\rangle_{L^2} = \int_M g\bigl((d\eta^{-1})U,(d\eta^{-1})V\bigr)\,\mu.$$
(By contrast, the analogous right-invariant $L^2$ metric on $D_\mu(M)$ is Arnold's classical metric whose geodesics are solutions of the incompressible Euler equations.)

Tasks:
(a) Exhibit a mechanical or continuum/fluid-type system whose configuration space is $D_\mu(M)$ and whose kinetic energy is given by $\tfrac{1}{2}\langle \dot\eta,\dot\eta\rangle_\eta^{\text{left}}$, so that the resulting Euler–Lagrange equations are the geodesic equations of this left-invariant $L^2$ metric.

(b) Derive the corresponding Euler–Arnold (geodesic) equation on $\mathfrak{X}_\mu(M)$ in terms of the right-logarithmic derivative, and interpret it physically.

(c) Determine whether there exist physically meaningful systems (in fluid dynamics, elasticity, plasma physics, or otherwise) that exhibit this type of left-invariance, as opposed to the usual right-invariance associated with material/spatial frame interchange.
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search reveals an extensive theory of the right-invariant $L^2$ metric on $D_\mu(M)$ (Arnold's framework for incompressible Euler flow) and of left-invariant metrics in image-matching/LDDMM contexts on full diffeomorphism groups, but no standard physical realization of an $L^2$ left-invariant metric specifically on the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group appears to be established. The question of identifying such a physical model appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Diffeomorphic Image Matching with Left-Invariant Metrics
status_evidence.snippet: Left-invariant metrics on diffeomorphism groups have been employed for image matching, but in the context of full Diff(M), not the volume-preserving subgroup.
status_evidence.claim: Left-invariant metric constructions exist on diffeomorphism groups but are typically used in image-matching, not as fluid models on $D_\mu(M)$.

status_evidence.title: Infinite-Dimensional Lie Groups and Algebras in Mathematical Physics
status_evidence.snippet: Geodesics of the right-invariant L2 metric on the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group are solutions of the Euler equations of ideal incompressible fluid mechanics.
status_evidence.claim: The physical model associated with the L2 metric on $D_\mu(M)$ is the right-invariant one (Arnold), making the left-invariant version a non-standard, unresolved analogue.
